name: Tawandê
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Eberhard 2009 (Mamainde grammar, pp. 21-31) subclassification discussion on Glottolog; no description of Tawande itself located.

sources.citation: Santana, Nelivaldo Cardoso. 2010. Descrição preliminar da nasalidade em Tawandê e comparação com outras línguas Nambikwára do Norte. Dissertação (Mestrado), Universidade Federal de Pernambuco, Recife. 74 pp. (supervisor Stella Telles). https://repositorio.ufpe.br/handle/123456789/7120
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: No stress-placement rule anywhere (every line with acento/acentuad-/tônic-/tom/tonal checked; ch.3 pp.35-45, ch.4, ch.6 pp.61-63 read). Stress is presupposed: all phonetic and phonemic transcriptions carry IPA primary (ˈ) and secondary (ˌ) stress marks, and the text repeatedly states that the oral/nasal vowel contrast holds only 'na posição do acento' / 'em sílaba tônica' while unstressed vowels nasalise optionally before a tautosyllabic nasal coda (pp.38, 42, 62). No tone analysis; only a Telles 2002 quotation (p.50-51) mentioning the 'suprassegmento tonal' of Northern Nambikwara speech.

sources.note: The only primary Tawandê corpus (last two speakers); any future stress statement for Tawandê would have to come from this archive or from a publication by Telles/Santana based on it. No published Tawandê phonology beyond Santana 2010 was found.

sources.citation: Telles, Stella. 2002. Fonologia e gramática Latundê/Lakondê. PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. xiii+398 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Not a Tawandê description, but the fullest phonology of the closest described sister languages (Latundê/Lakondê) by the linguist who recorded the only Tawandê corpus (2004, NEI-UFPE); its stress/pitch accent chapter (cited by Eberhard 2009:114,125-127 and summarised in Costa 2020 Quadro 71) is the analysis Santana 2010 tacitly applies when marking Tawandê stress. Would let a reader interpret Santana's stress marks; would not itself supply a first-hand Tawandê statement.
